stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec. Complex multi-platform live preview feature requiring elaboration of AC (openspec) followed by security/testability hardening around iframe sandboxing, XSS, real-time sync edge cases, and concurrent edit scenarios (speckit). High priority due to security surface area and cross-platform scope (GO, UP, MX).

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a new capability — ContentstackProvider currently holds content as a static value from getStaticProps and never updates it. The provider is the attachment point: subscribing to Contentstack's onEntryChange and updating context propagates to all 236 useContent consumers. Acceptance criteria were empty; VCs derived from the description and the identified attachment point.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so all ACs are new. I derived them from the story title/description, openspec's technical notes about the attachment point (ContentstackProvider + onEntryChange + useContent consumers), and the three-codebase scope. Key areas covered: (1) Core happy-path update propagation (AC-1, AC-8), (2) Environment gating so production is unaffected (AC-3, AC-14), (3) Race conditions with rapid changes (AC-2), (4) Error/resilience — connection loss, reconnection, malformed data, SDK absence (AC-4, AC-5, AC-6, AC-7), (5) Cross-site parity (AC-10), (6) Type/interface conformance (AC-11), (7) Subscription lifecycle — no duplicates, cleanup on unmount (AC-12), (8) Selective re-rendering (AC-13), (9) Unconsumed entry changes handled gracefully (AC-9). CAVEAT: I could not read the actual file contents of contentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, or useContent.ts. The ACs are based on the story description and file names alone. Once the implementer reads these files, criteria around the exact context shape, existing provider structure, and useContent return type may need refinement — particularly AC-11 (interface conformance) and AC-12 (subscription lifecycle), which assume patterns typical of React context + SDK integration.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. OpenSpec identified the technical attachment point (ContentstackProvider holding static content from getStaticProps, needing onEntryChange subscription to propagate to 236 useContent consumers) — this is concrete architectural elaboration that orients the implementer. Speckit then derived verification criteria from the story description and OpenSpec's technical notes, covering happy-path propagation, environment gating, race conditions, error/resilience, subscription lifecycle, and cross-site parity. The five verificationCriteria are all observable and testable: (1) published content on normal load, (2) live update without reload, (3) simultaneous multi-field/multi-entry updates, (4) session-end resilience with no blank areas, (5) revert behavior. Empty acceptanceCriteria with acceptanceChanged=false is expected brownfield behavior per policy and is not a defect. Manifest evidence confirms all four declared paths exist; per-codeline resolution shows all paths resolved (case_variant for gotransit context file, extension_variant for upexpress context file, all exact for metrolinx) with zero unresolved entries. Speckit's caveat about not reading file contents is excluded from scoring per instructions. The spec is ready to implement with ordinary open questions a competent writer resolves around exact context shape and useContent return type.
